canal-h1.title: 大运河
trans: China is big, and the north and south are far apart.
The fields in the south grow a lot of rice.
But people in the north could not get rice from the south, because the road was too far.
It took many days on foot, and the road was not safe.
The Sui emperor thought of a plan: dig a very long canal.
The canal ran from the south all the way to the north, and many people worked on it for many years.
When it was done, boats could sail from the south to the north.
Merchants took rice and many other things north by boat.
A boat is faster than walking, so goods got cheaper, and towns grew up on both banks.
People call it the Grand Canal; fourteen hundred years have passed, and people still use it today.

canal2-h1.title: 坐船游玩
trans: Last month, Mum and Dad took me out on a boat.
We got up at six, because it was a long drive.
At the river I saw many boats; ours was small but very clean.
When the boat set off, I was a little scared.
But the boat moved slowly and gently on the water, so I was not scared any more.
A breeze came across, and it was not hot at all.
I saw many fish in the water, and a few birds in the sky followed us the whole way.
At noon, Mum took out the food she had made that morning, and we ate while looking at the hills on both sides.
At three in the afternoon, the boat came back to the bank.
The day went by fast, and I still remember it now.

dongzhou2-h1.title: 猫和老鼠
trans: There was a cat and a mouse, and they lived in one big house.
Every day the cat wanted to eat the mouse, but the mouse ran very fast.
One morning, the cat waited for the mouse behind the door.
The moment the mouse came out, the cat jumped out.
The mouse was scared, ran out of the house, and ran all the way up the mountain.
The mountain path was too long, and the cat could run no more.
The cat sat at the foot of the mountain, looked up, and said nothing.
The mouse reached the top and saw water, flowers, and lots of good things to eat.
Best of all, there was no cat on the mountain.
The mouse said: "I will live right here, and I am not going down!"

han-h1.title: 丝绸之路
trans: In the Han dynasty, Chinese people did not know what lay to the west.
The emperor sent a man to go west and take a look.
He travelled for many years before he came back.
He said: "There are many countries in the west, and many new things."
When Chinese merchants heard this, they wanted to go west to trade too.
They carried silk, because people in the west loved silk.
The road was long, over mountains and through very hot places; one journey took a year or two.
Merchants from the west came too, bringing horses and new fruits.
Because the most famous thing on the road was silk, people called it the Silk Road.
This road joined China to places very far away.

han2-h1.title: 我的小猫
trans: We have a little cat at home; its name is Little White.
It is white, and only its eyes are black.
Every morning it wakes me up.
After I get up, the first thing I do is feed it.
It likes fish best, and when it has finished it goes to play with a ball.
Sometimes it jumps onto my books and goes to sleep.
With it on my books, I cannot read.
When I go to school, it watches me from the doorway.
When I come home, it runs over and gives a little cry.
At night it sleeps beside my bed; it is my best friend.

konfucius-h1.title: 孔子的学生
trans: More than two thousand years ago, there was a teacher in China called Confucius.
At that time, only people with money could go to school.
Confucius said: "Whoever wants to learn, I will teach."
So he had many students, grown-ups and children too.
They read together, talked together, and walked together.
Confucius said: "After you learn something, think it over often."
He also said: "If you do not know, just ask."
A student asked him: "What is a good person?"
He said: "What you do not want yourself, do not give to others."
Two thousand years have passed, and Chinese people still repeat Confucius's words.

ming-h1.title: 郑和下西洋
trans: In the Ming dynasty China had a very large fleet.
The man who led it was called Zheng He.
His ships were large — larger than a house.
There were many people on board, and many goods.
They carried silk, tea and many fine goods.
They set out from China and went west.
They reached many countries.
Some places were very hot, some very far.
People in other countries gave them new animals.
Zheng He made the voyage seven times in all.

ming2-h1.title: 奇妙的发现

sents.mn: to like; to be fond of
to know; to become aware of
to look; to watch; to read
to like; to be fond of
to like; to be fond of

to look; to watch; to read
to look; to watch; to read

trans: The Ming dynasty had two very famous men.
The first loved plants and trees.
He wanted to know which of them could be used as medicine.
He walked a great deal and saw many mountains.
He spent nearly thirty years and wrote a book.
The book held a great many plants and medicines.
The second loved walking, and looking at mountains and rivers.
He went to many places no one else had been.
Every evening he wrote down what he had seen that day.
Both men did the same thing: look closely, and write it down.

paper-h1.title: 纸的故事
trans: Long ago, China had no paper yet.
People wrote characters on bamboo.
Bamboo is heavy; one book took a lot of bamboo, and one person could not carry it.
In the Eastern Han, there was a man called Cai Lun.
He thought: "Could we make something light and cheap to write on?"
He put tree bark and old cloth in water and beat them into small pieces.
Then he made them into a thin sheet, and when it dried, that was paper.
Paper was light and cheap, and easy to write on.
With paper, students could carry books to school, and teachers could write down the lessons.
Later, paper went from China to many countries around the world.

paper2-h1.title: 书里的世界
trans: My favourite thing is books.
My room has many books, some new and some old.
Books are full of interesting stories.
Some books tell of things long ago, of Dayu and of the Great Wall.
Some books tell of the birds in the sky and the fish in the water.
When I read, it is as if I have gone somewhere far away.
Sometimes I read so intently that I do not even hear Mum calling me.
Mum says: "Reading lets you know so many things."
She also says I can ask her about any character I do not know.
I read for a while every evening, and I want to read even more.

print-h1.title: 印书的故事
trans: Once there was paper, people could write books.
But a book had to be written out one character at a time, and that took many days.
So books were few and expensive, and only people with money could afford them.
Later, someone thought of a good way.
They carved the characters into a block of wood.
Once carved, they put black ink on the wood, and then laid paper on it.
One press with the hand, and the characters were on the paper.
One block of wood could be used many times, so many books could be made in a day.
Books became cheap, and more people read.
Later this method reached other countries, and changed the world.

print2-h1.title: 图书馆的一天
trans: This afternoon, the teacher took us to the library.
The library is big, with a great many books inside.
The moment we went in, everyone stopped talking, because many people were reading.
The teacher said: "You may look for a book you want to read yourselves."
I found a storybook about long ago.
In it were emperors, the Great Wall, and a very long road.
I sat down, and once I started reading I read for two hours.
I read so intently that I forgot the time; only when the teacher called me did I get up.
I took three books home, and Mum said: "So many, can you finish them?"
I said: "I certainly can!"

qin-h1.title: 万里长城
trans: More than two thousand years ago, China had many small states that were always fighting.
Later, Qin Shi Huang defeated the other states and made China one country.
He was China's first emperor.
He made everyone in the country write the same characters and use the same money.
But people from the north often came to attack China.
So Qin Shi Huang had many people build a wall in the north.
They worked from morning till night; it was tiring and hard.
The wall ran along the mountains and took many years to build.
Because it is so very long, people call it the Ten-Thousand-Li Great Wall.
Two thousand years have passed, the Great Wall is still there, and today we can still go and see it.

qin2-h1.title: 爬山的孩子
trans: The weather is fine today, so the teacher takes us to climb the mountain.
We meet at the school gate at eight; twenty of us in all.
The mountain path is long, with trees on both sides.
We walk and talk at the same time, and we even see little birds.
After an hour of walking, I am tired and do not want to go on.
I sit under a tree and drink some water.
A friend comes over and says: "Almost there, keep going!"
I think for a moment, stand up, and walk on.
At the top, we shout: "We did it!"
Looking down from the mountain, the school looks as small as a dot.

qing-h1.title: 康熙皇帝

sents.mn: to like; to be fond of

trans: The Qing dynasty had a famous ruler called Kangxi.
He became ruler when he was very young.
He ruled for more than sixty years.
He got up very early every day to work.
He also loved learning new things.
He studied mathematics, and learning that came from the west.
People from the west told him about the sky.
He had a great map of China made.
At that time China was very large.
Many people say he was one of the best rulers.

qing2-h1.title: 故宫里的秘密

sents.mn: to look; to watch; to read

trans: In Beijing there is a very large and very old set of buildings.
People call it the Forbidden City.
It was built for a Ming ruler.
Inside there are more than nine thousand rooms.
The buildings are red and very beautiful.
The ruler worked in the largest room.
Many officials came to see him every morning.
There are many beautiful things inside as well.
There is writing, there are books, and things made of gold.
Today many people come here to look.

reform-h1.title: 改变的时代
trans: As the Qing dynasty was ending, China had many difficulties.
Countries to the west had new ships and new things.
Their ships were fast and large.
Many Chinese began to think: we must learn new things.
Young people wanted to learn western learning.
Some officials said China needed new schools.
They wanted new ships and new roads too.
Doing these things was not easy.
But they did not give up.
Their ideas shaped the China that came after.

reform2-h1.title: 变化中的上海

sents.mn: to like; to be fond of
to like; to be fond of

trans: A hundred years ago and more, Shanghai was still a small place.
Later, many ships came here.
People from many countries settled here.
They brought new things and new ideas.
The city had new schools.
And newspapers that came out every day.
At night the streets were still bright.
The old China and the new things were both here.
Some people liked it, some did not.
Shanghai’s change was China’s change in those years.

republic-h1.title: 新中国的梦
republic-h1.en: The Dream of a New China

sents.mn: to look; to watch; to read

trans: A little over a hundred years ago China still had an emperor.
Many people thought China should be different.
There was a man called Sun Yat-sen.
He had been to many countries and seen many things.
He said the country belongs to everyone.
He believed the Chinese people could do it.
Many young people worked with him.
In 1912 the new state began.
The new government set up new schools.
The road ahead was hard, but people still had hope.

republic2-h1.title: 新时代的年轻人
republic2-h1.en: Young People of a New Age
trans: A hundred years ago China had many young people.
They went to the new schools.
They studied mathematics, writing, and western learning.
Some went to other countries to study.
They saw many new things.
After finishing, many of them came back.
They became teachers, doctors, and workers.
They wrote new books and spoke in new ways.
They wanted to make the country better.
They said that study can change a country.

rider-h1.title: 草原骑手
trans: Far to the north of China lies a vast grassland.
There are no mountains there, only sky and grass.
Long ago, a people lived there called the Khitan.
The grassland was vast, so they were always on the move, and their homes could be taken up and carried away.
They learned to ride from childhood, and their horses were fast and fine.
Grown-ups and children alike rode very well.
They wanted to write their own language down, so later they made a writing of their own.
They traded with the Song in the south, selling horses and buying tea and cloth.
Sometimes the two sides fought, but trade never stopped.
They lived in the north for more than two hundred years.

rider2-h1.title: 草原上的风
trans: The wind on the grassland is strong, and it blows all year round.
When the wind comes the grass all moves, and from far off it looks like water.
The children who live here learn to ride when they are very small.
By three or four, they have a horse of their own.
In the morning they go out with the grown-ups and watch the cattle and horses.
They eat outside at noon, and only come back in the evening.
The night sky is dark, but the stars are very bright.
A city has so many lights that you cannot see a sky like this there.
They sing outside, and you can hear it from far away.
Life on the grassland is not easy, but they say: "This is our place."

sanguo-h1.title: 诸葛亮的智慧
trans: After the Han, China split into three states, called the Three Kingdoms.
The three states were always at war.
At that time there was a very clever man called Zhuge Liang.
Liu Bei asked him three times before he came out to help.
He could read the weather, and he was very good at finding a way.
Once, the enemy came, but there were very few soldiers in the city.
Zhuge Liang left the city gate open and sat alone on the wall, reading.
The enemy saw the gate open and thought: "There must be many soldiers inside."
They did not dare go in, and left.
Zhuge Liang served his state until he was very old, and people still tell his story today.

sanguo2-h1.title: 好朋友的力量
trans: I have three very good friends.
We are at the same school and in the same class.
Every day at noon, the four of us eat together.
Sometimes we think differently, but after we talk it is fine again.
Last month I got sick and could not go to school.
I was at home alone, and it was very boring.
On the third day, my three friends came to see me.
They brought fruit and books, sat by my bed, and told me what was happening at school.
I was so happy listening that I forgot I was sick.
The next day I felt much better; good friends really can help a person get well faster.

scholar-h1.title: 勤学的年轻人
trans: In the Jin dynasty, many different peoples lived in the north.
They spoke differently and wrote differently.
Because everyone had to work together, many young people began to learn Chinese characters.
They went to school very early every day.
The teacher taught them to read first, and then to write.
A character had to be written many times, and if it was not good, they wrote it once more.
Some were still reading in the evening; with no light at home, they sat by the door to read.
Once they had learned the characters they could do many things; some became officials, some became merchants.
They did not forget their own writing either, and knew both scripts.
They said: "A person who has studied can get on anywhere."

scholar2-h1.title: 学者的笔记
trans: In the Jin dynasty there was a man who loved to read.
His family had no money, but it had many books.
Every morning he read as soon as he got up, and he read every kind of book.
He had a notebook, and always kept it on him.
Whenever he saw something good, he wrote it down at once.
Year after year the notebooks grew, and he kept them in a big chest.
Later he grew old, his eyes were poor, and he could write no more.
He gave the chest to his students.
Many years later people were still reading these notebooks, because in them was everything he had seen in his life.
He once said: "If you do not write it down, you soon forget."

shang-h1.title: 骨头上的字
trans: Long ago, China had a dynasty called the Shang.
At that time there was no paper yet, so people wrote characters on bones.
The bones were big and white, and many characters could be written on them.
The Shang people believed there were gods in the sky.
When they had a question, they wrote it on a bone to ask the gods.
They asked: "Will the weather be good today?"
After asking, they burned the bone with fire.
Lines appeared on the bone, and they read the lines to find the answer.
These characters are China's earliest characters.
Later people found these bones in the ground, and today we can still see the characters on them.

shang2-h1.title: 市场的一天
trans: Today is market day.
In the morning, Mum and I go to the market together.
There are many people at the market; it is very lively.
Some people sell fruit, some sell fish, and some sell vegetables and meat.
The apples are very red, three yuan each.
I bought three apples and ate one; it was delicious.
Mum bought fish, vegetables and fruit.
There were too many things, so I helped Mum carry them.
We went home together, and Mum cooked the fish and vegetables.
Our whole family ate together, very happy.

shufa-h1.title: 写字高手
trans: More than sixteen hundred years ago, in the Jin dynasty, there was a man called Wang Xizhi.
He began learning to write when he was very small.
He practised every day and never stopped for a single day.
After writing, he went to the river to wash his brush.
He washed it for so many years that the water in the river turned black.
The characters he wrote were beautiful; some were like wind, some like water.
So people called him the "Sage of Calligraphy".
One spring, he met many friends in the mountains, and they wrote poems together.
He put everyone's poems together and wrote a few lines at the front.
Those few lines became the most famous writing in China, and today people still learn his way of writing.

shufa2-h1.title: 学写汉字
trans: This week, we started learning to write Chinese characters.
First the teacher taught us how to hold the pen.
She said: "Sit up straight, and only then do your characters look good."
We started with the two characters 水 and 山.
These two look easy, but writing them well is not.
A character has many strokes, and which one to write first matters.
I wrote one character more than thirty times, and it still was not good.
The teacher said: "Don't rush, write slowly."
I wrote slowly, and got better day by day.
I showed Mum my best character, and she put it up in her room.

song-h1.title: 中国的四大发明
trans: Chinese people made many useful things, and four are the most famous.
The first is paper; only with paper could people write books.
The second is the way of printing books.
Song people made the characters into separate small blocks, which could be used again after use.
The third is a small thing that shows direction.
Far from home at sea, people used it and did not lose their way.
The fourth is gunpowder.
At first, people only used it to make beautiful fire.
Later, these four things slowly reached other countries.
Many people say they changed the world.

song2-h1.title: 纸钱的故事
trans: Long ago, the money people used to buy things was made of gold.
This money was small, but heavy.
A merchant bought a lot at once, so he had to carry a great deal of money.
The money was too heavy for one person to carry, and the road was not safe.
Song people thought of a way.
They left the money in one place and took a piece of paper.
On the paper was written how much money it stood for.
Paper is light and small, easy to carry on you.
In another city, that paper could be exchanged for the money.
This let merchants travel further, and today many countries still use money made of paper.

tang-h1.title: 长安的繁华
trans: More than thirteen hundred years ago, China had a great dynasty called the Tang.
The Tang's biggest city was Chang'an, and at that time it was the biggest city in the world.
More than a million people lived there, and the streets were straight and long.
Because the Tang was so famous, people came from many countries.
Some came to trade, and some came to study.
They brought horses, fruit, and new music.
So people in the city could eat things that came from far away.
The Tang also had many famous poets, and the most famous was called Li Bai.
In those days, women could study, and could ride horses too.
Many people say the Tang was one of China's best times.

tang2-h1.title: 诗人看月亮
trans: The Tang dynasty had a very famous poet called Li Bai.
He travelled to many places and was often away from home.
One night he was staying away from home, alone.
When he got up, he saw the ground was all white.
He thought: "Is that water on the ground?"
He looked up at the sky, and only then knew it was the light of the moon.
The moon was big and bright.
Looking at the moon, he thought of his home far away, and felt a little sad.
He wrote a very short poem, only four lines, but everyone remembers it.
People away from home think of home too when they look at the moon.

tao-h1.title: 田里的诗人
trans: In the Jin dynasty there was a poet called Tao Yuanming.
When he was young, he was an official.
An official has money, and a name.
But he did not like it, because an official has to say things every day that he does not want to say.
One day he said: "I will not do this any more."
He went back to his own home and began to farm.
He grew vegetables, and planted many flowers too.
In the morning he worked in the fields, and in the evening he wrote poems.
In his poems he said: "In the fields, my heart is free."
His family was not rich, but he was happy, and today Chinese people still read his poems.

tao2-h1.title: 下雨天
trans: This morning, the moment I got up I saw the sky was dark.
A little later, it began to rain.
It rained hard, so I could not go out to play.
I sat by the window and watched the rain outside.
The rain hit the ground with a lovely sound.
People in the street were walking fast; a child ran past, soaked through.
I felt a little bored, so I got a book to read.
Mum made me a cup of hot tea and sat down to read too.
By the afternoon the rain slowly eased and the sky brightened.
Outside looked clean, and I thought: a rainy day has its good side too.

tea-h1.title: 一杯好茶
trans: Chinese people began drinking tea very early.
By the Song dynasty, tea was already an everyday thing.
Tea is made from the leaves of a tree that grows in the hills.
Before drinking tea, the water must first be boiled.
The water must be neither too hot nor too cold; with the wrong water, even good tea tastes poor.
Song people took their tea seriously.
They looked at the tea first, then smelled it, and only then drank slowly.
They said drinking tea is not only drinking.
Over tea, a person can sit down and talk slowly.
To this day, Chinese people still love drinking tea.

tea2-h1.title: 茶馆的故事
trans: Song cities had many teahouses.
A teahouse opened early, because many people came in the morning.
Some came to drink tea, some came to meet friends.
Merchants talked business here; old people talked of times long past.
Children came too, and sat at the back listening.
In the afternoon, a storyteller would come.
He told them so well that everyone fell silent.
In the stories were kings, soldiers, and dragons.
One story took several days, so everyone came back the next day.
The teahouse was also where you heard the news; in China today you can still find teahouses like that.

xia-h1.title: 大禹治水
trans: Long ago, a great flood came to China.
The flood went into the fields, and into many people's homes.
People had nowhere to live, and could only go up the mountains to live.
Dayu was a good man, so the king asked him to go and control the flood.
Dayu first looked at where the water came from, and then thought of a way.
He opened a road for the water, and let it flow away to the sea.
He worked together with many people, and every day was very tiring.
For thirteen years he did not go home.
Three times he walked to his own door, and did not go in.
Later the water went down, people went home, and everyone said Dayu was very good.

xia2-h1.title: 小龙学游泳
trans: There was a little dragon, and it could not swim.
Every day it watched the other dragons playing in the water.
It stood by the river; the river water was very deep and very cold.
It did not want to get into the water; it only wanted to watch from the bank.
Mother said: "Don't be afraid, you can do it! Come, I will teach you."
Mother swam first to show it, and the little dragon slowly got into the water too.
It tried once, twice, three times, and still had not learned.
It did not give up, and came to learn every day.
A month later, the little dragon had learned to swim.
Today the little dragon plays in the water with its friends, very happy.

yuan-h1.title: 马可·波罗来华
trans: More than seven hundred years ago, China had a great dynasty called the Yuan.
The great khan of the Yuan was Kublai, and his realm reached from the east far into the west.
In those days the roads were safer than before, so more people travelled.
A young man set out from Italy; his name was Marco Polo.
He travelled with his family, crossing mountains and very hot places, and it took more than three years to reach China.
After reaching China, he lived in Dadu for seventeen years.
He saw many cities and many people.
He said China's cities were far bigger than those of his own country, and that people here even used money made of paper.
After going home, he told others what he had seen, and someone wrote it into a book.
Because of this book, Europeans learned of the world to the east for the first time.

yuan2-h1.title: 元朝的美食
trans: In the Yuan dynasty, people came to China from many places.
So the food in China grew much more varied.
People from the north ate lamb from childhood.
They also drank a kind of tea with milk in it, white and hot.
A cup of it in cold weather warmed a person up at once.
Merchants from the west brought new things; some were fragrant and could be put in meat.
Once added, the meat tasted quite different.
People in the south still preferred rice and fish.
So one country had many kinds of good food, and in a big city you could eat things from far away.
Marco Polo wrote down what he had eaten too, and said his own country had nothing like some of it.

zhou-h1.title: 天命的故事
trans: After the Shang, China had a new dynasty called the Western Zhou.
The Western Zhou king said: "It is Heaven that made me king."
He said that Heaven is always watching every king.
If a king does well, Heaven lets him stay king.
If a king does badly, Heaven no longer lets him be king.
So a king must love the people, and the people will love the king too.
In those days, many people worked in the fields.
The weather was good, and the crops in the fields grew well.
There was rice at home, and meat too, and life was good.
China at that time was very big and very beautiful.

zhou2-h1.title: 大树下的朋友
trans: There is a big tree at the school gate.
That tree is very tall and very old.
My friends and I play under the big tree every day.
When the weather is nice, we read under the tree.
We play games, tell stories, and are very happy.
My friend can tell many lovely stories.
Today he told a very long story, and we all laughed.
The teacher came and said: "Time for class!"
We all said: "Goodbye, big tree!"
We ran into the classroom and started class.
